notes: Expected returns are a 50/50 blend of the sample mean and a menu-beta heuristic.

Every mix below the frontier has exactly its column's risk and is the most diversified mix found at that risk for its return level: a local search from several starting points, not a proof that no better mix exists.

The balanced point is where, going down the column, diversification stops rising faster than return falls, each measured as a share of what the column offers; the peak is the most diversified mix found at that risk.

One-year ranges are the 2.5th, 50th and 97.5th percentiles of 2,000 one-year paths resampled from the mix's own daily history in runs averaging 21 days, recentred on the expected return, at constant weights.

One-year ranges under the volatility model are the same percentiles of 2,000 one-year paths in which each fund's volatility follows the pattern fitted to up to ten years of its daily history and the funds' shocks are replayed together from days they all share, centred and scaled to this view's expected return and risk.
